In triangle $PBT$ the same ratio applies with the larger angle $34^\circ$: $\tan 34^\circ = \frac{BT}{32}$, so $BT = 32\tan 34^\circ \approx 21.58$ m.

$h$ is opposite the angle $56^\circ$ and we know the hypotenuse, so we use sine: $\sin 56^\circ = \frac{h}{7}$.
$h = 7\sin 56^\circ \approx 5.8$ cm.

Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

canonical_solution.text_md: Sketch a right-angled triangle for each position of the boat. The height of the cliff is opposite the angle of elevation and the distance from the boat to the bottom of the cliff is adjacent to it, so use the tangent ratio each time.
First position: $\tan x_1 = \frac{10}{45}$, so $x_1 = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{10}{45}\right) = 12.53^{\circ}$.
Second position: $\tan x_2 = \frac{10}{14}$, so $x_2 = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{10}{14}\right) = 35.54^{\circ}$.
The angle of elevation increases by $x_2 - x_1 = 35.54^{\circ} - 12.53^{\circ} = 23.01^{\circ}$, which is $23.0^{\circ}$ correct to one decimal place.

Round to two decimal places: the height of the tower is $12.74$ m.
